rows.title: Minimal fix/mix nucleus
rows.boundary: The explicit recursive Interaction calculus has a total finite observer, an unbounded inductive operational semantics, soundness/completeness, stable observations, divergence correspondence and related-carrier transfer. It supports heterogeneous inherited carriers and delayed values. Arbitrary Scheme programs are outside the stated calculus. Call-by-need caches carry evaluation proofs indexed by the exact program; completed source errors are shared. Active cycles are separate runtime diagnostics. Mutable writes reset the cache and advance the generation. Every finite operational value/error derivation completes at some machine budget from any sound warm cache. Completed results and cycles are stable under increasing budgets; reported cycles prove divergence. Certified instance and mutable reads retain the exact request/snapshot divergence proof. Exhaustion alone remains inconclusive. Actual safe C3 methods now accept parameters and preserve final-self and delayed inherited calls, including argument forwarding. The existing recursive machine shares the complete method name/argument request, reports parameterized cycles with divergence proofs, and distinguishes changing-argument recursion from a repeated request. Dynamic argument equality is computable and kernel justified. Existing value-only object observations are preserved at every depth by the request reindexing theorem. The declared Interaction compiler now executes through the existing unsafe sharedFix/instantiate constructor, records native demand traces, and uses a total safe checker to reconstruct exact-program evaluation proofs and compare reported values/errors. Shared demand executions and safe Evaluates derivations are equivalent; bounded recordings agree at every source depth, and every finite derivation has an admitted trace. A sequential private-cell operational model proves current-body identity, installation before forcing and exactly one constructor start for every ready heap. Checked native C3 field/method reads transfer to existing plan and source graph derivations. These native closures share construction rather than request results. No unchecked unsafe fixed-point equation is assumed. The existing sharedFix now executes one source-owned SharedCell.tie constructor program, also interpreted by a pinned Lean 4.34.0 sequential Ref/Thunk primitive model. Every successful primitive step and trace refines the private-cell protocol. The installed reference remains the result thunk, every ready result has exactly one constructor start, and the self forwarding thunk reads the private Ref at most once. Closure return and completed native publication are separate observations. An optional IO observation adapter records actual closure entries/returns, private Ref pointer readbacks and completed cold/hot gets; safe admission joins those operation data with the current-program result receipt. Valid operation data establishes the declared model derivation, not authentication of IO origin. C++ primitive/reference-counting/compiler/concurrent-memory verification and arbitrary unchecked callbacks remain separate; no opaque IO law is added.

Applicability equals current-argument filterMap on every call. Sound candidate caches preserve complete value/arity-error outcomes and remain sound under lookup, touch and LRU eviction. Successful registration, contribution and predicate registration invalidate the old candidate cache. These are universal kernel laws for the concrete typed generic. Typed registration, per-context selection and cache controls; not a formal resolution of every cross-library extension/conflict policy in the discussion. Explicit watched-absence admission and guarded provider transactions now implement the proposed negative-assumption policy. Refusals retain the actual first present factory, its absent prefix and candidate transaction proof. Acceptance is complete for final transaction snapshots preserving all watched absences; disjoint edits rebind the old certificate. The provider-transaction gate retains its fixed graph; changed topology uses the verified migration gate below. Graph migration now compiles the actual target topology/root, retains complete surviving-name overlays, installs new names and finishes all target edits. All explicit negative and positive constraints are checked on that exact target. Same first winning identities plus disjoint target ancestry/key edit scopes prove complete preparation equality, retaining arbitrary joint proof and hot context data; changed selections require fresh admission and a cold slot. Complete capability acceptance and certified availability are kernel laws. The context/key/value family and computation stay fixed during migration; arbitrary-language hidden assumption inference and machine cost claims remain open. Finite pure Computation syntax now automatically infers value/presence reads and required/forbidden guards through nested helpers and both branches. Universal execution congruence and capability safety are kernel laws. Analyzed graph migration checks the expanded positive/negative policy on the actual completed target and proves complete acceptance. Stable known observations preserve computed values/errors, result proofs and exact context-hit decisions; hidden-read changes invalidate the computed slot even when explicit capability selection is stable. Presence-only observations need availability equality, not function equality. Affected or unknown callbacks require fresh result admission and an empty computed slot. Unknown callbacks receive no automatic capability-safety guarantee; conservative branch contracts may be unsatisfiable. Arbitrary-language closure/effect/termination inference and machine costs remain open.

rows.title: Appendix B method fragments
rows.boundary: Universal standard-combination correspondence for every monad and arbitrary method callbacks: ordered before methods, the nested primary next chain, reversed after methods and nested around wrappers. Ordered fragment append laws preserve next chaining; callbacks may suppress or repeat next. Existing user combinations and forwarding controls remain typed operations. No CLOS syntax adaptation is required.

rows.title: Appendix B generalized lens constructor
rows.boundary: lensGen implements getter/setter/wrapper and skew-focus laws exist. The paper itself calls full generalized prototypes future work; no claim that all such semantics are closed. Functional view composition and narrowing preserve consumer observations and proofs; these projections complement the prototype lens construction and do not implement a universal dynamic MOP.

rows.title: Appendix C type notation

rows.title: Appendix D fixed-point functions
rows.boundary: Shared/rebuilding unsafe thunks remain executable alternatives. The safe recursive calculus supplies sound/complete finite observation, unbounded return/error semantics, divergence characterization, and least-information refinement against any fixed observation. Native shared execution is checked through the declared interaction compiler; no arbitrary unsafe-thunk equivalence is claimed. The safe shared evaluator provides proven memo receipts, cold-slot laziness, cached errors and active-path cycle diagnostics; concurrent instance reads serialize on a mutex. Every finite operational value/error derivation completes at some machine budget from any sound warm cache. Completed results and cycles are stable under increasing budgets; reported cycles prove divergence. Certified instance and mutable reads retain the exact request/snapshot divergence proof. Exhaustion alone remains inconclusive. Actual safe C3 methods now accept parameters and preserve final-self and delayed inherited calls, including argument forwarding. The existing recursive machine shares the complete method name/argument request, reports parameterized cycles with divergence proofs, and distinguishes changing-argument recursion from a repeated request. Dynamic argument equality is computable and kernel justified. Existing value-only object observations are preserved at every depth by the request reindexing theorem. The declared Interaction compiler now executes through the existing unsafe sharedFix/instantiate constructor, records native demand traces, and uses a total safe checker to reconstruct exact-program evaluation proofs and compare reported values/errors. Shared demand executions and safe Evaluates derivations are equivalent; bounded recordings agree at every source depth, and every finite derivation has an admitted trace. A sequential private-cell operational model proves current-body identity, installation before forcing and exactly one constructor start for every ready heap. Checked native C3 field/method reads transfer to existing plan and source graph derivations. These native closures share construction rather than request results. No unchecked unsafe fixed-point equation is assumed. The existing sharedFix now executes one source-owned SharedCell.tie constructor program, also interpreted by a pinned Lean 4.34.0 sequential Ref/Thunk primitive model. Every successful primitive step and trace refines the private-cell protocol. The installed reference remains the result thunk, every ready result has exactly one constructor start, and the self forwarding thunk reads the private Ref at most once. Closure return and completed native publication are separate observations. An optional IO observation adapter records actual closure entries/returns, private Ref pointer readbacks and completed cold/hot gets; safe admission joins those operation data with the current-program result receipt. Valid operation data establishes the declared model derivation, not authentication of IO origin. C++ primitive/reference-counting/compiler/concurrent-memory verification and arbitrary unchecked callbacks remain separate; no opaque IO law is added.
